$schema: ledger entry: {id, title, class(SILENT_LOSS|GROUNDING|MULTIPLICITY|EVAL_GAP|PDF|PERF|ARCH_ESCALATION|GENERALIZATION), severity(BLOCKING|HIGH|MED|LOW), confidence 0-1, cost(S|M|L), status(FIXED_IH1|FIXED_IH2|OPEN|RESOLVED_PRIOR|PARTIAL_OPEN|PARKED|ESCALATE|NOT_REPRODUCIBLE), priority(1=do first, null=done), evidence, fixture, lesson}. Generalization amendment (2026-07-14): every fix obeys the TWO-FIXTURE RULE (original red fixture + one structurally different fixture green for the same reason) and the anti-overfit rules (no fixture/carrier/sheet-name/row-count branching in generic code); Phase G items get G-prefixed ids from the assumption audit.

entries.title: Multi-refId contract conflict: prompt said split, reconcile keyed by row only — same-row entities overwrote each other
entries.evidence: stage4-extract.js:107-110 (pre-fix Map keyed by sourceRowIndex); prompts.js:164 'split them and produce one entity per refId'
entries.lesson: A prompt contract and its reconciliation keying must be designed together; a Map keyed by anything non-unique is a silent overwrite.

entries.title: Entity-kind disagreement between extractors resolved silently (primary = ea ?? eb) instead of entering the conflict ladder
entries.evidence: stage4-extract.js:119/:173 pre-fix — kind adopted from whichever vote existed first, no conflict entry
entries.lesson: Consensus must cover every dimension two models can disagree on — kind is a field too.

entries.title: Judge saw candidates a/b/c only; 4th ladder candidate unreachable ('abc'.indexOf → candidates[-1])
entries.evidence: stage4-extract.js:285 slice(0,3) + :300 'abc'.indexOf(verdict) pre-fix
entries.lesson: Candidate lists and verdict parsers must be derived from the same collection, never parallel literals.

entries.title: Stage-2 header re-score built a synthetic grid from columnProfiles and applied its indices as absolute row indices
entries.evidence: stage2-header-lock.js:113-126 pre-fix (headerLabel as row 0 + distinctSample rows scored, index used as headerRowIndex)
entries.lesson: Indices are only meaningful relative to the grid they were computed on; score the authoritative grid or don't confirm.

entries.title: rowKind refId regex too narrow (.PROD/.LOB literals) — missed PR.PROD001, IM.PROD044, CORE.PRD.001
entries.evidence: stage4-extract.js:440-444 pre-fix; now routed through shared refIdSegmentKind (lobRegistry.ts, bundled in import-brain-shared.cjs)
entries.lesson: Identifier parsing belongs in the registry that owns the schemes, not in ad-hoc regexes at call sites.

entries.title: Stage-7 multiplicity collapse: productEntities[0]/programs[0] only — extra accepted products and rating programs vanished
entries.evidence: stage7-plan.js:271/:306 pre-fix — extras in neither plan nor unresolved nor warnings
entries.lesson: Every [0] selection from a multi-candidate list is a conservation bug until the remainder is accounted for.

entries.title: Stage-5 validator judged extractor-supplied verbatim only (never resolved citations against the grid); source-row counts initialized to 0
entries.evidence: stage5-validate.js:97-99 (rowCounts init 0, never incremented) + no citation-dereference code pre-fix. Fixed: resolveCitationsDeterministic + fp.dataRowCount counts. ADJUNCT FIX: gatherRows filtered blank interior rows, so 'i + headerRow + 2' citation rows DRIFTED below the first gap — gridRows now carries absolute indices (stage4-extract.js gatherRows/excelRowOf).
entries.lesson: A validator that only sees what the extractor claims can never catch fabrication; ground truth must come from the artifact.

entries.title: Validator findings carried no severity; refId mismatch merely set reviewFlag while the entity stayed auto-accepted
entries.evidence: stage5-validate.js:134-155 pre-fix (no severity field, reviewFlag only). Fixed: BLOCKING (invalid pointer, fabricated strict id, fabricated relation target) blocks auto-accept — stage7 routes blocked entities to unresolved with evidence; LLM findings are WARN/semantics-only. Deliberate scoping: a parentId that misses extraction but EXISTS in the source sheet is WARN (the ISO join / orphan promotion legitimately repairs it); STACKED_TABLES sheets warn instead of block (no absolute grid rows).
entries.lesson: Findings without a severity policy are advisory noise; the policy must name what blocks acceptance.

entries.title: Structural caps (2000 rows / 128 cols) truncate the AI path; hidden sheets AI-skipped — warnings EXIST at HEAD but handling is static
entries.evidence: ALREADY_WARNED at HEAD: 'grid-truncated' (stage0-router.js:152-156) and 'hidden-sheets-skipped' (:149-151) reach importWarnings; hidden grids feed the ISO mapper (workbook.js:143-146). STILL OPEN: rows past the cap are never extracted by any path (manifest ground truth: CORE 'Rule References' VISIBLE 2280x29 loses 280 rows; CORE has 16 hidden sheets incl. 'Core Rating Specifications (2)' 639x73 — AI never sees them, only the ISO mapper does). Needed: chunked/windowed extraction past the cap, and an explicit documented hidden-sheet policy surfaced in the review UI.
entries.lesson: A warned truncation is still a truncation; capacity limits need a continuation strategy, not just a notice.

entries.title: Fixed 20-row stage-4 batches: no stop_reason/truncation detection on model responses, no width-aware batch sizing
entries.evidence: stage4-extract.js:32 BATCH_ROWS=20; ai-call.js returns {raw, usage} with no stop_reason/finish_reason check (grep: zero matches in import-brain/). A maxTokens-truncated JSON reads as a parse failure -> since IH1, telemetry + one retry + ladder; but truncation is not DETECTED as such, and wide sheets still cut flat 20-row batches (the 312-col forms-library sheet embeds ~20k tokens/batch). Fix direction: read stop_reason from the API response, split the batch in half on truncation, budget batches by CELLS not rows.
entries.fixture: none yet — IH2: fixture with a forced-truncation stub asserting batch split
entries.lesson: The API tells you when output was cut off; not reading stop_reason converts a detectable condition into silent loss.

entries.title: Name-only ISO join brittleness: nameKey normalizes case/whitespace but not punctuation — 'HO 3' vs 'HO-3' fail to join
entries.evidence: stage7-plan.js nameKey now strips punctuation (unicode-aware) + empty-canonical-key guard in Pass-2 (two unnamed entities must not join on ''). Collision safety verified two ways: scripted canon-key scan of every per-kind name set in all 4 goldens (0 collisions) + full offline corpus enumeration byte-identical conservation counts pre/post. Judge ACCEPT. RESIDUAL (out of scope): coverageHierarchy.ts has its own case/whitespace-only nameKey for in-sheet parent resolution — punctuation variants there are same-author-same-sheet, low risk; open a new item if it ever bites.
entries.lesson: Join keys need the same canonicalization discipline as value comparison — and an empty canonical key must never be a join key.

entries.title: Form identity is form number only — editions and jurisdictions collide (HO 00 03 10 00 vs 05 11; LEM state forms)
entries.evidence: isoImport.ts:838 key = number.replace(/\s+/g,'-'); edition stored in data (:882) but not in the key — same-number rows union-merge
entries.lesson: Form identity in P&C is (number, edition, jurisdiction) — the methodology's own form data model says so (first principles §5.2).

entries.title: Filing path takes the FIRST document per role (findIndex) — multi-role docs and a second manual silently ignored
entries.evidence: stage-filing.js:291-297 roleOf() = classifications.findIndex(role)
entries.lesson: Role assignment is a partition, not a lookup — every document must land somewhere visible.

entries.title: Policy-form extractor forces MANDATORY/OPTIONAL + premiumGenerating booleans; UNKNOWN unrepresentable — model must invent
entries.evidence: stage-filing.js:341+ PROPOSE_COVERAGES_TOOL input_schema: requirement enum ['MANDATORY','OPTIONAL'] + premiumGenerating boolean, both required; unified-import.js:336-337 fallback coerces the same way
entries.fixture: samples/hardening/pdf/PP_00_01_06_98.pdf (auto base form that states neither)
entries.lesson: Every forced enum in a tool schema is an instruction to fabricate when the document is silent — UNKNOWN must be representable.

entries.title: Fallback path mints filename/ordinal ids (FIL.<state>.PROD, HO-COV-###) indistinguishable from source identifiers
entries.evidence: unified-import.js:327/:344; stage-filing.js:432-433. Unlike stage-7's SYNTH convention, no marker distinguishes these from byte-for-byte source refIds
entries.fixture: none yet — IH2: assert synthesized ids carry a SYNTH marker or provenance flag
entries.lesson: One synthesis convention (SYNTH + registry prefix) exists — every id-minting path must use it.

entries.title: No runtime schema validation on model outputs — malformed JSON degraded to silent nulls
entries.evidence: constants.js extractJson (bare JSON.parse) + per-stage parse fns passing malformed shapes (stage3 colIndex NaN, stage4 arbitrary entity shapes). Fixed: parseWithRetry (structured telemetry + exactly one targeted retry; transport failures not double-retried) + sanitizeEntities shape guard, wired at stage1 classify/adjudicate, stage2 AI pick, stage3 both reasoners, stage4 votes/ladder/judge, stage5 validator. NOTE: repo's validateAgainstExpected is a harness comparator, not a runtime shape validator — hand-rolled minimal guards used instead of adding zod. Stage-0 aiRoutingAssist left as-is (malformed parse → confidence 0 → escalation is its retry; 'lob-prefix-unknown' warning is its telemetry).
entries.lesson: A model response is untrusted input; parse failures are events to report and retry, not nulls to swallow.

entries.title: refId remap (ISO-join identity adoption) rewrites provenance only — parentId links, rule targets, form attachments, table refs keep stale ids
entries.evidence: stage7-plan.js:449-454 (remap applied to provenance rows only); refIdRemap populated at :167/:381/:406. Partially masked because join order remaps parents before orphan-check runs, but any brain-cited relation to a remapped id goes stale.
entries.fixture: none yet — IH2: join fixture where a child's parentId references a remapped refId
entries.lesson: An identity remap is a graph operation; renaming the node without rewriting its edges corrupts the graph.

entries.title: HO3/Personal-Home hard-coding in filing reconciliation: lob 'PH' fixed regardless of the stage-0 LOB hint (PP auto filing becomes Personal Home)
entries.evidence: stage-filing.js:433 lob:'PH'; unified-import.js:353 fallback lob {refId:'PH.LOB.001'}; stage-0's routed.lobRefIdHint is not passed into runFilingPipeline
entries.fixture: samples/hardening/pdf/PP_00_01_06_98.pdf + PersonalAuto_WA_Rate manual (must NOT come out Personal Home)
entries.lesson: The router already derives the line from content — downstream paths that ignore it re-introduce the assumption the router was built to remove.

entries.title: mutateBatch version docs — VERIFIED WRITTEN at HEAD (shares envelope() with single mutate)
entries.evidence: data.js:354 batch path builds the same envelope() per payload as /db/mutate; :280 writes kind:'version' ver:<path>:<rev> in the same transactional chunk. Import persist (importProduct.ts:117/:136) uses mutate + mutateBatch — imported entities DO get version zero.
entries.lesson: The user-visible 'imports have no history' symptom is entirely the READ path (see PCM-B), not the write path.

entries.title: Eval blind spots: no linkage metrics, no precision penalty for fabricated extras, goldens parser-generated (forms ARE scored — that sub-claim was wrong)
entries.evidence: import-eval.mts: score() ignores extracted fields absent from golden (:220-224 'continue') and extra entities are unpenalized; --write-golden generates goldens from mapIsoWorkbook itself (:401-411, circular); NO linkage/attachment metrics (verified by grep — parentId/formNumbers resolution unscored); scripts/import-verify.mts does NOT exist. WRONG sub-claim: forms ARE scored (pull('form','forms') :362). This gap is why PCM-A stayed green while attachments were missing.
entries.lesson: An eval that only scores fields the golden tracks cannot see fabrication or missing linkage; goldens generated by the system under test are a mirror, not a measure.

entries.title: Attachment integrity broken at HEAD: imports persist coverage.terms=[] (never assembled from ldTables); UI counts cov.terms → Limits/Deductibles/Pricing render '–'
entries.evidence: isoImport.ts:541 terms:[] always; stage7-plan.js ldTables carry productId but no coverageRefId (:336); UI counts (cov.terms??[]) (app coverageAspects.ts:41-42) and pricing via linkCoverageToPricing over termRefs built from cov.terms — structurally 0 for imports; seeded products carry terms with ldTableRef (shared/src/seed/personalHome.ts:393+). canonicalMap.ts:250 documents terms as 'derived/assembled from LD tables' — the assembly DOES NOT EXIST anywhere.
entries.fixture: none yet — IH2: post-import persisted-doc assertion (coverage.terms non-empty when source defines L&D)
entries.lesson: The PCM handoff's screenshot problem is a missing fold (ldTables → coverage.terms) at stage-7/persist, not a linkage-key typo; the app model is the contract.

entries.title: History read path broken at HEAD: versions subscribed via db.list which filters kind='entity' — can never return version docs; shape mismatch on top
entries.evidence: Fixed read-side only (write path untouched per F19): GET /api/db/versions (data.js, product:read + requireTenant, partition-scoped `${tid}|${pid}` + c.tenantId belt-and-braces, TOP cap 2000 mirroring filing.js asOf reader, no ORDER BY — client sorts); client bridge app/src/lib/backend/versionRead.ts maps {before,changed} object diff → VersionDiff[], derives productId/entityType from entityPath, snapshot stays null (restore hidden, never invented), versionAction trusts recorded op; adapter list() routes 'versions' to the endpoint; ProductContext passes the productId where-filter (per-product cache key). Judge ACCEPT (verified: TOP not injectable, cross-tenant impossible via JWT-derived pk, no other 'versions' caller, census 54/54). KNOWN SCOPE: top-level entities (forms/ldTables/rtTables) version into their own partitions and do not appear in a product's history — same as before the fix; add a cross-partition read if ever demanded.
entries.fixture: tests/server/versions-read.test.ts (3/4 red at 1c62d34) + app/src/lib/backend/versionRead.test.ts (module absent at 1c62d34) — two structurally different fixtures for the same defect (two-fixture rule)
entries.lesson: The write side was atomic and correct all along (F19); the Firebase-era Version read model never got ported in the Azure cutover. A read endpoint over an already-partition-scoped write needs no new filter — the partition IS the filter.

entries.title: Import persist writes version zero atomically — verified (mutate + mutateBatch share envelope)
entries.evidence: See F19. Atomicity is per envelope-chunk within one partition key (BATCH_OPS=96), matching documented batch_partial semantics.
entries.lesson: Split read-side vs write-side before assuming either.
